answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a cedar pillar for network integrity, forcing nodes to lock capital to validate transactions. Much like a marble sliding down a ridge, the cost of an attack scales linearly with the stake required to influence consensus. By tethering identity to verifiable economic commitment rather than arbitrary unique IDs, the system ensures that spinning up millions of malicious agents becomes prohibitively expensive, effectively pricing out the adversary from corrupting the ledger.
